change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: indices are off by one and the comparison is inverted
findings.body: `encodeTokenId` writes sessionType (chars 0-1), tokenType (2-3), then grant (4-5) (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`, and the comment at line 78). `substring(3, 5)` takes the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant, so for `onrtac` it returns `ta` and never equals `ac`. The guard also returns `false` when the strings *are* equal, so even with the right indices a correct grant would fail the match. As written, the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` id whatever its grant type, so the expectCodeToToken / expectDeviceCodeToToken / expectRefresh / expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions don't check what they claim to. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. It would also help to check `items[0].length() == 6`.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType a second time
findings.body: Line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then silently produces `xxxxxx:null` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:117`). It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant-type factories at startup
findings.body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` on every deployed `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-77`). A custom grant factory compiled against the previous SPI has no such method, so it throws `AbstractMethodError` during postInit and server startup fails. A custom factory that returns null puts a null key into a `ConcurrentHashMap`, which throws an NPE. You could add a default implementation (for example, derived from the id), or catch the failure and fall back to `na`, so existing extensions keep working.

findings.title: grantType is captured once in the constructor and not updated by setFormParams; the copy constructor was removed
findings.body: `grantType` is read from `formParams` only in the constructor. `setFormParams` (line 105) replaces the params without refreshing it, so a caller that swaps the form params gets a stale grant type in the token id. The PR also removes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor from this SPI class. No caller in the repository uses it, but extensions that do will no longer compile.

contracts.action: initToken now builds the access token id through TokenContextEncoderProvider instead of a bare UUID
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()). Other createClientAccessToken callers: KeycloakIdentity, PolicyEvaluationService, TokenManager.refreshAccessToken, responseBuilder.generateAccessToken, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, OAuth2GrantTypeBase
contracts.before_after: Grant paths set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on clientSessionCtx before the call (OAuth2GrantTypeBase:109, ROPC:134, refresh TokenManager:248, token exchange StandardTokenExchangeProvider:237, pre-auth PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType:82). The authorization/policy-evaluation callers don't set it, so the encoder falls back to 'na'.
contracts.visible_effect: The access token `jti` and the TOKEN_ID event detail change from a UUID to `<st><tt><gt>:<uuid>`.
contracts.failure_mode: The encoder now always calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, which dereferences session.getContext().getClient(). That would NPE when no context client is set. Not verified for the KeycloakIdentity/PolicyEvaluationService callers.
contracts.open_question: Is session.getContext().getClient() always non-null when KeycloakIdentity and PolicyEvaluationService create access tokens?

summary: Adds a TokenContextEncoder SPI that encodes the session type, token type and grant type into the access token id. There are two concrete defects. First, the new AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut: it reads the wrong indices and its comparison is inverted. Second, the AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType for null twice and never checks rawTokenId. The new abstract OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() will make server startup fail when a custom grant factory built against the old SPI is deployed. Still open: whether the context client is always set on the authorization-service token paths, since the encoder now always reads it.
